Round 18 — the whole page, six compositions

Rounds 13 and 14 are settled and say so themselves: npm run round13 is retired, and npm run round14 throws at this page because the composition it priced is shipped — the page carries data-slot="PS-5". Rounds 15 (vertical rhythm), 16 (the club name) and 17 (the header bar) are taken, so this round is 18: plan ids are append-only and never renumbered. It asks the question the current page raises — one plate below the fold, and 847px of unmarked vertical space in 8 runs. What closes that emptiness: art moved, art added, art paid for less, or air taken back? Six compositions of the same built page, each photographed whole at one display factor, from the load that produced its numbers (D160). Nothing here touches src/: applying a composition is a separate commit set, after the ruling.

Question 1 — which composition?

Answer in letters (e.g. “1C”), and say if a mix is meant.

A — the page as it stands. The incumbent, and the baseline every other row is a delta from: hero column stacking a 376x307 plate over the 376x235 mark, the reasons section, ONE capped horizon plate between it and the schedule, the schedule, and the ink footer. Measured here as 8 empty runs over 28.5% of a 2973px page, with a 569px gap before the band — so the weakness this round is about is not the hero, it is the middle.

B — the plate closes the page instead of dividing it. Same plate, same cap, same bytes: the whole horizon section moves below the schedule, so the page reads reasons → schedule → plate → footer. The words keep their order and the band stops being the seam the eye crosses on its way to the dates. Page height barely moves — this is not a height answer, it is an answer about where the emptiness lands, and check:space prints exactly that as empty runs.

C — the mark closes the page, the plate owns the fold. The two graphics in the hero column get one job each, and the identity moves out of the fold: the mark walks to the ink footer and is repainted for a dark ground (its `stroke-rule` hairline and its accent are both under the 3.0 graphic bar on ink — 2.97 for the accent, D116 — so the repaint is part of this option and check:render prices it), and the hero plate gets the column’s full height at the shipped crop recipe. That is the widest honest window on the leaf the page is allowed one of, so the colour bill is the point of this row.

D — the reserved join slot gets a second plate now. PS-3 is a reserved media column in the schedule card that measures **544x0** today: the round-10 ruling named the place, the club photo that will fill it is MS32, and nothing ships there. This row asks what the page looks like if a licensed archive leaf stands in it while the wait is still open — the 1903 Euclid plate the repo already builds and does not paint, at the slot’s measured box, which is a 0.53x downscale of its own scan and keeps 67% of the drawing. Colourless line work, so the colour bill barely moves; the cost is page at the widths where the grid is one column.

E — the band pays less page. Keep the one plate and shrink the window on it: the cap moves from the scan’s 698px to 520px, so the leaf paints 520x261 instead of 698x351 and the band gives the page back a hundred-odd pixels where the column is wider than that. Hairlines go down instead of up — the one thing D347’s cap was protecting still holds — and the widths where the cap never binds (a 390 column is already 358) pay nothing, which is why the phone column is printed and not assumed.

F — no new art, less air. Close the emptiness without buying a pixel of colour: the below-fold sections and the margins inside them come off one step of the spacing scale, so the page reaches the dates sooner and its colour census stays where it is. This is the row that tests the assumption the last four rounds made implicitly — that emptiness is answered with pictures rather than with less of the thing that made it.

The pages, one scale

Same document, same factor, whole page — top to bottom. This is the comparison: rhythm, weight, and where the page puts its one coloured thing. The last column is 390, because the phone is where a desktop delta lies.

The heroes, closer

What the measurements say

  • Emptiness is the question this round asks, and a percentage flatters a page that grows, so compare pixels. At 1240 the shipped page carries 8 empty runs over 28.5% of 2973px = 847px of unmarked vertical space. This run: as-shipped 847px (28.5%, +0 page), plate-closes-the-page 847px (28.5%, +0 page), identity-closes-the-page 1020px (32.4%, +174 page), reserved-slot-gets-a-plate 847px (28.5%, +0 page), band-pays-less 845px (29.3%, -90 page), no-new-art-less-air 682px (24.3%, -168 page). The least empty here is no-new-art-less-air at 682px.
  • Page height: every option's cost is printed at all 4 widths, because a desktop delta has been a lie before — round 13's option C was "+0" at 1240 and +314px at 390 (D161). The cheapest page here is no-new-art-less-air at 2805 (-168); the most expensive is identity-closes-the-page at 3147 (+174).
  • Colour is the budget being spent, not a mood: one coloured slot is the ruling (D149-1b/2b), so the column is what each composition asks for. Shipped is 0.393% of pixels at chroma ≥ 0.08; the cheapest option is as-shipped at 0.393% and the loudest is identity-closes-the-page at 0.559%.
  • Gates: every option is green on `check:render` at 1240/640/390/320 — these are compositions to choose between, not breakage to fix.
  • Resolution: every plate in this run paints at or below its own scan width — no upscaling, so the hairlines are the archive's drawing shrunk, not interpolated.
  • The phone, priced separately (D161): at 390 the shipped page is 4122px, and the answers to what the band costs there are phone-shipped +0, phone-desktop-only -313, phone-short-leaf -53.

How this was made

npm run round18 (design/round18.mjs): mutate dist/client/index.html per option — a <style> block of attribute selectors, DOM moves, plates planted as data URIs through design/grill/plate-crop.mjs, the same recipe that built the shipped hero asset — then run the gates CI runs. Options live in design/grill/round18-options.mjs; this file is generated from design/grill/round18/report.json and throws on a missing lookup. A design round, not a gate: it runs in no CI.
